findings.claim: If lock release fails, writer() skips closing the descriptor after clearing its reference to it. The process can keep the lock indefinitely, blocking subsequent appends and torn-entry recovery until it exits.
findings.repro: On POSIX, inject a one-shot OSError in _unlock before it calls flock. Append at position 0 and observe the error after the log and head have been committed. Restore _unlock and attempt an append at position 1 from a fresh CaseLog on the same path while the first process remains alive. The leaked descriptor still holds the lock, so the append raises CaseLocked.

findings.claim: The CLI relies on filesystem access and does not enforce the producer's claimed case-root ownership check. The cited file-mode test only covers files created by the writer.
findings.repro: Create a case under one OS account, grant a second account read and traversal access to the case directory and read access to the log and head, then run cma case check as the second account. It exits 0 and prints the entry count and head hash even though the caller does not own the case root.
